To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adrenergically mediated stimulation of hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis is mediated through α 1 -receptors in control animals, through β-adrenergics in the early phase of liver regeneration, and through α 1 again in the later stages.
during the process which follows partial hepatic resection, there is a transition, first in the type and later in the sensitivity of the adrenergically stimulated hepatic metabolic pathways.
the type of adrenoceptor involved in the metabolic action of epinepherine changes from β to α 1 as the animal ages or the liver regenerates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of adrenergics in the process of liver growth.

the changes that occur in adrenergically regulated hepatic metabolism during the process of regeneration which takes place after partial hepatecotmy and with the changes that take place in the liver as the animals ages.
a study of the role of the adrenergics in liver cell regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adrenergically induced hepatic metabolic responses are mediated by different receptors during the course of liver regeneration and aging.
the adrenergically mediated metabolic effects in the liver are mediated by different adrenergic receptors at different stages of liver regeneration.

in liver cells formed after hepatectomy, the type of adrenoceptor involved in the hepato-adrenergic response changes from α 1 to β and back to α 1, and that the number of α 1 receptors does not change, while β-adrenergically mediated cyclic AMP accumulation is enhanced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adrenergically mediated metabolic responses of liver cells are dependent on the type of adrenoceptor present and that these receptors change in a time- and stage-dependent manner during the process of regeneration which follows partial hepatotomy.

during the process liver regeneration there is a transition from β- to α 1 -receptor involvement in the metabolic actions, and that the β-receptors seem to be more sensitive to adrenergic agonists than the α 1 ones.
the α 1 /β-adrenergic receptor transition observed during the process of regeneration and aging is not related to the changes in the cyclic AMP system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a dynamic organ in which adrenergic receptors change during the process of regeneration.
during the process that follows partial hepatection there is a shift in the adrenergically-mediated metabolic responses, from α 1 to β and back to α 1.
the type of adrenoceptors involved in the hepato-cellular response to epinephrine is different depending on the stage of liver regeneration and/or aging.
